prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout of an indoor room: a bright foreground window wall and potted plant stand on the far left (about 0.8–1.5 m away), a child seated in a highchair in the lower-left foreground (roughly 0.8–1.2 m away, nearly within the camera wearer's arm's reach), a tall hutch against the left-center wall (about 2.0–2.5 m away), an open doorway on the right leading into a recessed room (4–6 m deep, shown nearly black), and a woman in the lower-right foreground (about 1.0–1.5 m from the camera wearer and 1.2–1.5 m to the right of the child). Across frames 1 to 4, the camera pans slightly right and the woman straightens up from a downward-angled posture to face the camera wearer directly, while in frame 5 the camera pans back left so the woman is mostly cut off at the right border and the child and left-side plants re-enter full view. Unlike the dark, shadowed RGB doorway and dim lower foreground, the depth map clearly separates the foreground silhouettes of both the child and the woman from the mid-ground hutch and deep doorway behind them. However, the depth map is unreliable on bright light sources—rendering the ceiling light fixture at the top right of frames 2–4 and the blown-out window glare on the left of frames 2–4 as maximally bright (near) artifacts—and merges the child's lower body with the highchair tray into an indistinct white blob.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few discrete foreground and background regions across the five frames: the potted plants on the left window ledge in frames 1, 2, and 5 (about 1.0–1.5 m away, above and left of the child), the woman in the lower-right foreground in frames 1–4 (about 1.0–1.5 m away), the child in the lower-left foreground only in frame 5 (about 1.0 m away, facing downward with hands near their mouth), and a tiny 'chair' fragment beside the woman in frame 3. Across frames 1 to 4, the woman's segmented mask shifts from a leaning profile partially clipped at the bottom-right edge to an upright head-and-shoulders silhouette facing the camera wearer, before disappearing in frame 5 when the camera pans left and she is occluded by the right frame boundary. This map makes the exact pixel boundaries of the woman's torso and the left-side plant cluster stand out against the cluttered room, which is harder to parse at a glance in the dim RGB frames. However, the segmentation is highly unreliable: it misses the child completely in frames 1–4 and the woman in frame 5, fails to detect the tall hutch, highchair, and hanging garments within arm's reach of the wall, and persistently misclassifies the distant windows inside the dark background doorway (4–6 m behind the woman) as a 'tv' in every frame.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the five-frame strip, detecting only a single yellow upper-body skeleton for the woman in the lower-right foreground of frame 3 (located roughly 1.0–1.5 m in front of and slightly to the right of the camera wearer). In that third frame, five facial keypoints (eyes, nose, and ears) and a horizontal shoulder bar show that her torso is squared to the camera and her head is oriented directly toward the camera wearer, with her body below the shoulders cut off by the bottom edge of the frame. While the RGB strip shows the child in the lower left (about 1 m away, holding their hands up to their mouth within their own arm's reach) and the woman across all five frames as the camera pans right and then back left, the pose map provides quantitative confirmation of her frontal head and shoulder alignment only at the midpoint of the sequence. The map is otherwise heavily unreliable due to severe false negatives: it fails to detect any body or magenta hand skeletons for the child across all five frames (whose lower body is occluded by the highchair and frame edge) and loses the woman's pose in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5 despite her face and shoulders being clearly visible in frame 4.
